title: Credibility assessment of explicit FEA for deployment force in a transcatheter delivery system: ASME V&V40 application across two models and two mechanisms
device: Transcatheter delivery system for a self-expanding peripheral stent

models.name: Model 1 — Lesion-Crossing Dynamics (explicit FEA)
models.what_it_computes: Peak advancement force and force–displacement profile while advancing the delivery sheath across a stenotic, partially calcified segment; local vessel wall strain at the lesion contact.

models.name: Model 2 — Sheath Retraction and Release (explicit FEA)
models.what_it_computes: Transient force spike and steady retraction force during sheath withdrawal for device release; contact stick–slip behavior and energy dissipation at the device–sheath–vessel interfaces.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism A — Lesion Crossing
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Controls operator push force needed to traverse stenoses; excessive force risks vessel injury, plaque dislodgement, or sudden jump with malposition.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism B — Sheath Retraction for Release
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines deployment force spikes that can induce axial device shift and wall trauma during release, affecting placement accuracy and safety.

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All credibility factor scores are reported on a 0–12 scale (0 = none, 12 = excellent), with acceptance threshold set at 8 for each model×mechanism pair.
